collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A friend tells a villager carrying coconuts on their hip to carry them on their head: thank them and walk on, or try it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is carrying a heavy basket of coconuts on (subject.his/her) hip, the way (subject.he/she) always has. (friend) falls into step beside (subject.him/her). "You know, if you carried it on your head, it would be much easier on your back. Here, let me show you..."

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Thank you," says (subject), "but I like it this way." (friend) looks a bit put out. "But it's better on your head." "Maybe," says (subject). "I still like it this way." (subject.He/she) keeps walking. (friend) walks with (subject.him/her) for a while, clearly wanting to say more, and then, with a visible effort, doesn't.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) tries it on (subject.his/her) head. It's terrifying. The basket wobbles, the coconuts rumble, and (subject) walks like a heron for twenty steps before the whole thing comes down. Coconuts everywhere. (friend) helps pick them up. "It takes practice," (friend.he/she) says. "Then I'll practice another day," says (subject), and puts the basket back on (subject.his/her) hip.
